rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance of combining RNA and image modalities. This tests the impact of fusion method (concat) and aggregation (none) as foundational choices. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is critical for prioritizing further exploration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with concat fusion (config_016) achieve 52.6% validation accuracy. This experiment tests weighted fusion instead of concat, clarifying whether fusion method impacts performance. It directly builds on the previous multimodal setup, exploring a key design choice (fusion type) with minimal additional complexity, balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction and exploration of critical components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have similar validation accuracy (0.526 vs 0.523). This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice) with avgpool aggregation (a new method not yet tested in this setup), clarifying whether profile settings and aggregation methods significantly impact performance. It balances exploration of critical design choices while building on previous multimodal experiments.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve the highest accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_019) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion methods on multiprofile tasks. It directly builds on the strongest existing configuration while exploring a critical design choice with potential for improvement.

Existing evidence shows that for multiprofile settings, using avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (config_019: 0.639 accuracy) is highly effective. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) while keeping the high-performing avgpool+weighted setup. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder further improves performance, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a critical component.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion (config_019: 0.638999 accuracy) and avgpool aggregation are strong performers. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (a more complex method) with weighted fusion could further improve performance, while keeping the same RNA and image encoders. It directly addresses the uncertainty around aggregation methods' impact on accuracy, which is critical for optimizing the model architecture.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) maintains performance under the same optimal settings, clarifying if RNA encoder choice is critical. It balances exploitation of proven settings with exploration of potential improvements, avoiding redundant tests of inferior configurations.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high performance (config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with a more powerful model (imagenet_vit_l) further improves performance while maintaining the effective RNA encoder and fusion strategy. It clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on multimodal performance, a key design decision with uncertain optimal value.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high validation accuracy (e.g., config_037: 0.706). This experiment tests whether switching from avgpool to transformer aggregation (a key design choice) with the same RNA and image encoders could further improve performance. It directly extends the promising direction of config_037 while exploring a critical uncertainty about aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile configurations with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (another advanced encoder) while keeping transformer aggregation and weighted fusion would further improve performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice, a key design decision, and explores a promising direction without repeating prior configurations.
